subject.title: fix(cron): route failure alerts to thread ids

question: Should OpenClaw accept `failureAlert.threadId` as a public cron config/protocol/CLI/storage surface once this PR is rebased, documented, and live-proven?
rationale: The implementation direction is plausible, but it creates a new public cron field and CLI flag plus a persisted SQLite projection, so automation should not treat product and compatibility acceptance as implicit.

options.title: Accept After Rebase And Proof
options.body: Require conflict resolution, account-id docs, and redacted live Telegram proof, then accept the additive failure-alert thread surface.

options.title: Accept Local Proof Only
options.body: Maintainers may choose to accept the local persistence, unit, schema, storage, and gateway evidence while owning the remaining live Telegram uncertainty.

options.title: Defer The Public Surface
options.body: Pause this PR and keep the linked issue open until a maintainer decides the permanent cron alert-routing contract.

recommendation.title: Accept After Rebase And Proof
recommendation.body: Require conflict resolution, account-id docs, and redacted live Telegram proof, then accept the additive failure-alert thread surface.

likelyOwner.reason: This is the best available owner signal from CODEOWNERS plus prior work around the sibling Telegram topic-routing behavior.
